correctness.rationale: For any compactly supported invariant Borel probability under L(x,y)=(1+y-a|x|,bx), integrability gives E[y]=b E[x], hence 1=a E|x|+(1-b)E[x]. Writing P=E[x_+], N=E[x_-], m=P-N yields A P+B N=1 with A=a+1-b>0 and B=a+b-1>0. Since A+B=2a, direct substitution proves x_+-m=2aN/A and m-x_-=2aP/B, where x_+=1/A and x_-=-1/B are exact fixed points. For endpoint equality N=0 or P=0, support lies on one closed half-plane; L is an invertible homeomorphism for b>0, so the compact invariant support is two-sided invariant. The affine branch matrices M_+=[[-a,1],[b,0]], M_-=[[a,1],[b,0]] have characteristic polynomials t^2+at-b and t^2-at-b. Their values at t=0,±1 show exactly one stable and one unstable real eigenvalue under the stated inequalities; bounded bi-infinite branch orbits are fixed. Thus endpoint equality yields the corresponding Dirac atom; every other invariant probability has both signs. The source proof mistakenly attributes exclusion of -1 to A and +1 to B for M_+ (the correct evaluations are p_+(1)=A, p_+(-1)=-B), but both required inequalities hold and the stated hyperbolicity and theorem are valid. Independent SymPy algebra and an exact mixed-sign 2-cycle confirm calculations but are not substitutes for the general proof.
